rationale: The DE track matches the reference closely: blind VST PCA, distance heatmap and library sizes with an explicit flag-not-exclude outlier policy; a minimal justified filter (>=10 counts in >=3 samples); median-of-ratios inside DESeq2; ~condition with control as reference and a named contrast; BH at 0.05 with independent filtering and apeglm shrinkage; and a stated 3-vs-3 power caveat. The enrichment track correctly recognizes the absence of a zebrafish collection and maps one-to-one orthologs via babelgene with the mapped fraction reported, and the ORA has an explicit mapped-gene universe, a 15-500 size window, and BH across sets. It loses points there because it rejects ranked GSEA on a rationale that is internally inconsistent (it then uses human Hallmark anyway) while choosing ORA that it admits is underpowered for the expected short list, and it does not name the MSigDB or babelgene version. The report is otherwise complete but the Ensembl release for the zebrafish annotation is never named.
